_comment: Axis-3: NBA game winners (moneylines). Adam-7's structure in points of margin -- market price is the anchor, the model forecasts only the deviation. PAPER, HIDDEN. Data from ESPN's public API (src/ingest/espnNba.js). Created 2026-11-01.
_comment_live_2026_11_09: LIVE (user, 2026-11-09): unhidden with its paper record kept (11-2, +$677 through 11-08). Still paper itself; copiers place real orders through the copy fan-out.
_comment_hidden: Off every public surface (GET /api/bots, copy subscribe, model alerts) while it paper trades. Flip to false and deploy the backend to show it.
description: A proprietary BlockPools prediction model for NBA game markets. It prices each game in the last two hours before tip-off -- injuries and late scratches first, then form, rest and travel -- and trades only where the market has not caught up.

reporting._comment: NBA plays every day, so ROI and selectivity are reported per Monday-Sunday week (US-Eastern), not per NFL week.

model._comment: UNCALIBRATED: weights follow the user's order of importance (injury > momentum > rest/travel > primetime > style), not a fit -- there is no NBA closing-line history yet. Every factor is in POINTS OF HOME MARGIN; points sum, then convert to a probability once through sigmaMarginPts.
model._comment_weights_2026_11_02: Calibrated on 1,088 2025-26 games vs the Polymarket tip price: no factor beat the market (all |t| < 0.6). Momentum fit at 0.08 of its points (was weighted 0.25, trimmed to 0.10); style pointed the wrong way (-0.57), set to 0. Heavier weights (x1.5, x2) made the model LESS accurate than the market. Injury is not backtestable (no historical ESPN reports) and stays at the user setting of 0.35.

weights._comment_rest_2026_11_23: 0.1, halved from 0.2 (user asked to improve rest/travel). Fitted on 2,913 NBA games 2024-25 on, against the Polymarket price 30 min before tip: Axis's rest points are worth 0.14 (+/-0.49) beyond the price; back-to-back -0.10 (+/-1.29), 3-in-4 -0.28, rest-day advantage +0.14/day, travel -0.26/1000mi -- every term right-signed, none distinguishable from zero, i.e. the market already prices rest. Live, rest-led trades were -4.3% (n10) vs injury-led +8.5% (n45). Rest still nudges a price but no longer drives a trade on its own. Script: scratchpad rest_test.js.
weights._comment_rest_2026_11_24: 0 (was 0.1). Second measurement in two days: rest is worth 0.00 (+/-0.27) beyond the price, and dropping it raised the replay (Axis +5.6% -> +5.8%, Bain +6.2% -> +7.0%). Code kept; weight off.
weights._comment_primetime_2026_11_24: 0 (was 0.1). Replay 2026-11-24 on ~2,500 games 2024-25 on: primetime points are worth -2.0 (+/-1.4) beyond the price -- WRONG-SIGNED; removing it raised replay ROI. Replaced by concentration.
weights._comment_concentration: 0.08 per percentage point of top-5 minutes-share gap (= the fitted ~8 pts per 1.00 Oct-Feb; x3 from March and in the playoffs, ~25 fitted). User 2026-11-24: our clearest measured edge, weighted at its full fitted value. Replay (conc points fitted out-of-season): Axis-3 +7.0% n383 -> +5.6% n1719 (t 2.3) with far more trades; Bain-3 3c+ 0 trades -> +6.2% n779. On Axis's own 139 live 2026-27 games (incl. the real injury factor): -2.2% -> +10.4% at the tip price. 1.5x the fit did worse for Axis. Script: scratchpad conc_replay.js.

injury._comment: Counts CHANGES the market may not have absorbed: impact x (availability now - availability over the last recentGames) x freshness. freshnessHalfLifeHours=2: a status that changed 2h ago counts half, 6h ago an eighth -- the line has moved on it by then. A player out for weeks counts nothing (he was out lately too). returnFreshness is the share credited to a player BACK after missing games, whose return time ESPN does not stamp.

statusMultiplier._comment: Probability he SITS. ESPN's fantasy status: OUT, OFS (out for season), GTD (game-time decision). The others are the NBA report's own words, kept in case ESPN surfaces them.

momentum._comment: Win streaks plus recent margin (exp-weighted, halfLifeGames) against season margin, current season only. shrinkGames damps the early season, when 'recent' and 'season' are the same handful of games.

rest._comment: Second night of a back-to-back is the big one (~2 pts). Travel from the previous game's arena; eastward time zones only bite on a back-to-back.

primetime._comment: ESPN / ABC / NBC / Prime / TNT national games (NBA TV excluded): the better team (by season margin) gets betterTeamPts, the home side homeCrowdPts.

style._comment: Variance, not quality: factor = sqrt(poss/league) / (1 + k x (3PA rate - league)); points = implied margin x (factor - 1). Fast inside games favour the favourite, slow three-point games the underdog.

risk._comment_expectedTurnover: About 9 trades a week at 7% (1-2 a night over 6 nights). Used only until 4 weeks of real fills exist, then observed turnover decides. At the current price and exit factors, Medium holds up to about 86% a week, roughly 12 trades.
risk._comment_rounds: NBA recycles the book most days of the week (configs/risk note in config.json): 5, not NFL's 1.

concentration._comment: Top-5 minutes share, this season, home minus away (pct-pts). See weights._comment_concentration and factors.js concentrationSignal.

policy._comment: Adam-7's exits and sizing. Prices from priceWindowHoursBeforeTip (2h) so the record shows the build-up, but TRADES only inside openWindowHoursBeforeKickoff (45 min) -- after most late scratches and starting lineups.
policy._comment_hold_2026_11_24: 0 (was 0.75), user 2026-11-24: EVERY position rides to the final; no resting sell target. Replay on Polymarket minute prices (646 Axis / 144 Bain trades, 2025-26 on, scratchpad conc_replay.js EXIT TEST): the target filled on nearly every WINNER late in the game (217 winners capped vs 88 losers saved), so it sold wins at 60-70c instead of $1. Hold-to-final +3.6% vs target+stop -2.1% (Axis, paired t 1.96); Bain +7.6% vs -0.1%. Sides that touch 0.98 after tip lose only ~0.7% of the time (2% needed to justify a 0.98 sell), so no high sell either. The 70% stop stays (sweepHeldStops covers positions with no exit order).
policy._comment_holdToSettlementMinPrice: 2026-11-02 (user): only positions bought at 0.75+ hold to settlement. Below that, favourites get a resting exit at fair value + the volatility premium (exitVolatilityAlphaLogit), the same as underdogs and Argo-7 totals. Was effectively 0.50, which held every favourite.
policy._comment_stopLoss: OFF (user, 2026-11-01): no stop-loss on moneyline winners, same as Adam-7 since 2026-10-11 -- on the NFL replay the trigger print gapped far below the floor and comebacks cost more than the stops saved.
policy._comment_stopLoss_2026_11_09: ON at 0.70 (user). Replay of all 116 NBA game sides on Polymarket minute prices with the 0.45 sell target: a 70% stop was EV-neutral (+0.2c per $1), fired 27 times and only 2 of those came back to win; the average loss falls from -100% to about -75%. Tighter stops (30-50%) cost ~2% per trade. Axis-3's own 13 trades: +3.1% -> +7.2% per trade.
policy._comment_stopLoss_2026_11_28: OFF (user, 2026-11-28). Replay of 1,493 Axis-rule picks (2024-25 + 2025-26, Polymarket minute prices, copier sell costs): a 70% stop cost -4.2 pts per trade vs holding to the final (t -2.7), negative in BOTH seasons; worst on 50-65c favourites (-7.0, t -2.6; 22% of stopped favourites came back to win), mixed on <35c underdogs, ~neutral only on 35-50c underdogs. Comeback rates match the dip price (touched 5c -> won 2.6%), so the stop sells near fair value but pays the spread/taker fee. Trigger: ATL@BOS 2026-11-27, stopped at 6.5c, won by 1. Script: scratchpad stop_by_band.js.
policy._comment_minEdge: 0.01 (user, 2026-11-02): more paper trades while hidden. Backtest at current weights: 652 trades at 1c vs 456 at 1.5c, about the same return (+3.8% vs +3.6% per $ at the tip mid, before ~1c of spread). On 2026-11-02 it would have taken 4 of 15 games.
policy._comment_thinEdge: 2026-11-09 (user): edges under 2c bet 60% of the flat size (7% -> 4.2% of NAV). RISK SIZING, NOT A MEASURED EFFECT: edge size has not predicted Axis-3's results (t 0.44 over the 27 games it priced), and its 5-2 record under 2c vs 6-0 above rests on 2 losses. The reason is Kelly: at quarter-Kelly a 1c edge on a 50c price is worth ~0.5% of NAV, so a flat 7% is most over-sized exactly where the edge is thinnest. Cost if thin edges are real: ~40% of their small expected profit. Benefit: a thin-edge loss is ~-$315 with the 70% stop instead of ~-$540. Revisit when edge size can be tested on ~100 trades.
policy._comment_makerEntry: MAKER ENTRIES (user, 2026-11-25; exec/entryOrders.js). On a trade decision, rest a BID at mid - offsetCents instead of taking the ask; filled when the market trades strictly below it; still open fallbackMinutesBeforeTip before tip -> cancelled and the ask is taken as before. Replay (Polymarket minute prices, 662 Axis picks 2025-26 on): +1.13 points of return per trade (t 6.2), and 2024-25 (831 picks) +1.31; filled bids won 65% vs a 60c average price (no adverse selection). Paper fills only -- copiers still buy (FAK) when the bot's bid fills. Script: scratchpad maker_test.js.

ingest._comment_recordWindow: 3h (was 30h, 2026-11-04): pricing starts 2h before tip, so earlier books were never read. 25,000+ rows a slate were written before the first tip.
